meta.note: Curated from Google Scholar with links/abstracts. Citation counts are kept only to order papers within a year — they are not shown on the site. `npm run sync:scholar` pulls new papers into a side file.

publications.title: Symbolic Grounding Reveals Representational Bottlenecks in Abstract Visual Reasoning
publications.venue: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning (CoNLL 2026), co-located with ACL 2026
publications.abstract: Demonstrates that multimodal reasoning pipelines fail on abstract spatial tasks not for lack of downstream reasoning capacity, but because perceptual encoders drop relational geometry at the grounding bottleneck — motivating native visual-state interfaces over brittle language intermediaries.

publications.title: Concept Cues Reshape Human Verification in Bongard-LOGO Visual Reasoning
publications.venue: CVPR Workshop on Knowledge-Intensive Multimodal Reasoning
publications.abstract: Studies how explicit vs. implicit visual concept cues shift verification accuracy and response criteria in abstract visual reasoning, informing reliable human-in-the-loop and agentic verification workflows.

publications.title: Beyond the Linear Separability Ceiling: Aligning Representations in Vision-Language Models
publications.authors: Enrico Vompa, Tanel Tammet, Mohit Vaishnav
publications.abstract: A linear probe on a VLM’s raw visual embeddings sets a diagnostic baseline that separates weak perception from weak reasoning on compositional visual tasks. Most models fall short of it; pairing contrastive representation alignment with next-token training reorganizes visual state so models clearly surpass the ceiling.

publications.title: A Cognitive Paradigm Approach to Probe the Perception–Reasoning Interface in VLMs
publications.abstract: Adapts controlled cognitive-science paradigms into diagnostic evaluation workflows that isolate perceptual encoding failures from downstream reasoning errors in frontier vision-language models.

publications.title: Not How You Think, It's What You See: Decoupling Perception from Reasoning
publications.abstract: Shows that scaling test-time reasoning chains cannot recover spatial relations discarded during early visual encoding, arguing for perceptual-first architectures in multimodal agents.

publications.title: GAMR: A Guided Attention Model for (Visual) Reasoning
publications.abstract: An active-vision cognitive architecture that solves relational visual problems via closed-loop sequences of internally guided attention shifts and working-memory routing — learning reusable visual routines sample-efficiently and generalizing zero-shot to unseen tasks.

publications.title: PhD Thesis: Exploring the Role of (Self-)Attention in Cognitive and Computer Vision Architecture
publications.venue: Université Paul Sabatier (Toulouse III) / Brown University / ANITI
publications.abstract: Investigates how selective attention and working memory enable compositional visual intelligence — analyzing Transformer self-attention, establishing a computational taxonomy of visual reasoning, and introducing the GAMR active-vision architecture.

publications.title: A Benchmark for Compositional Visual Reasoning
publications.authors: Aimen Zerroug, Mohit Vaishnav, Julien Colin, Sebastian Musslick, Thomas Serre
publications.abstract: Introduces Compositional Visual Relations (CVR) to measure sample efficiency, out-of-distribution generalization and rule compositionality — exposing the data-efficiency gap between passive deep networks and active human perception.

publications.title: Understanding the Computational Demands Underlying Visual Reasoning
publications.authors: Mohit Vaishnav, Remi Cadene, Andrea Alamia, Drew Linsley, Rufin VanRullen, Thomas Serre
publications.abstract: Characterizes the computational demands of abstract visual reasoning across the SVRT challenge, establishing a taxonomy of same-different vs. spatial-relation routines and demonstrating how spatial and feature attention unlock the hardest relational tasks.

publications.title: Conviformers: Convolutionally Guided Vision Transformer
publications.authors: Mohit Vaishnav, Thomas Fel, Ivan Felipe Rodríguez, Thomas Serre
publications.abstract: A compute-efficient convolutional vision transformer with PreSizer resolution scaling that processes fine-grained high-resolution imagery without quadratic memory blowup — setting state-of-the-art results on Herbarium 202x and iNaturalist 2019.

publications.title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Identify Fossil Angiosperm Leaves at Family Level
publications.authors: Ivan Felipe Rodriguez, Thomas Fel, Gaurav Gaonkar, Mohit Vaishnav, Herbert Meyer, Peter Wilf, Thomas Serre
publications.venue: Geological Society of America — Abstracts with Programs · Leaf Lens project (Serre Lab, Brown University)
publications.abstract: Leaf Lens: an interactive explainable-vision workflow showing how neural networks organize morphological concepts across plant families to assist palaeobotanists in fossil leaf identification.
